newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ONGC says oil well catches fire.
newsitem.headline: India's ONGC says oil well catches fire.

text.p: India's Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) said a fire broke out on Wednesday in one of its oil wells in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh.
"There is a blow-out," an ONGC official in the Indian capital told Reuters by telephone. "We are still assessing the extent of damage."
The official said the fire broke out at 1:30 p.m. (0800 GMT) in an oil well in Mandapetta area, about 350 km (215 miles) east of the Andhra Pradesh capital Hyderabad.
United News of India said the blaze erupted during drilling, and flames leapt 55 feet (17 metres) in the air amid billowing clouds of smoke.
The news agency said police evacuated the residents of two nearby villages.
ONGC is India's largest state-run oil exploration and drilling firm.
